tasks.short: Communicate with one student by their chosen method.

steps.what: Read the method card before this student session.
Communicate with students who use an alternative method of communications, using sign language or computer technology.

tasks.design: A classroom colleague writes a method card before the session. The card holds the room, the method title, and one topic title. The speech-language pathologist still communicates with the student by sign language or the student's own technology. If the card has no row, the pathologist reads the paper method list inside the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The preferred method sat in a folder the pathologist opened at the start of a rare session.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper method card with the room, the method title, and one topic title is enough to start. No system is required.
tasks.still_hard: Following the student's signs and answers still takes the whole session.
tasks.human_edge: Only the pathologist can follow the student in the moment and answer in the student's method.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the method. The pathologist still communicates with the student.

reach.task: Start a session in the student's own method
reach.learn: A method card names the method. It does not speak for the student.

reach.task: Open a hearing session with the right method
reach.learn: The conversation stays with the person in the room.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the room, the method title, and one topic title shortens the search when the row is there. The speech-language pathologist still communicates with the student. Model knowledge.

Health data are a special category. The method card holds the room, the method title, and one topic title, not the student's health fact. This paper card is not software. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: A classroom colleague writes the method card before the session.
Fields are the room, the method title, and one topic title.
The card does not hold a health fact.
The pathologist communicates with the student in s2 at full time.
If the row is missing, the speech-language pathologist reads the paper method list inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because a classroom colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a recording or scoring tool is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this classroom already keeps a one-line method card for each student.
research_questions: How often a first session has no row on the method card.

incremental.description: No extra pathologist upkeep. A classroom colleague keeps the method card.
A classroom colleague writes the method card: room, method title, and topic title.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The session is the first one, so the method card has no row and the pathologist reads the paper method list. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct one speech or hearing study and report it.

steps.what: Read the topic card before this study.
Conduct or direct research on speech or hearing topics.
Report findings for use in developing procedures, technologies, or treatments.

tasks.design: A library colleague writes a topic card before the study. The card holds the topic title, the shelf, and the report date. The speech-language pathologist still conducts the research and writes the findings report. If the card has no row, the pathologist reads the paper topic list inside the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The topic and the shelf sat in a folder the pathologist opened at the start of a rare study.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper topic card with the topic title, the shelf, and the report date is enough to start. No system is required.
tasks.still_hard: Judging the sources and writing what the findings mean still take the study.
tasks.human_edge: The pathologist decides what the sources support and what the report should say.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the topic. The pathologist still conducts the research and writes the report.

reach.task: Start a hearing study from a named topic
reach.learn: A topic card names the shelf. It does not judge the sources.

reach.task: Write a findings note after a small study
reach.learn: The findings report is still written by the person after the study.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the topic title, the shelf, and the report date shortens the search when the row is there. The speech-language pathologist still conducts the research and writes the findings report. Model knowledge.

Health data are a special category. The topic card holds the topic title, the shelf, and the report date, not the finding. This paper card is not software. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: A library colleague writes the topic card before the study.
Fields are the topic title, the shelf, and the report date.
The card does not hold the finding.
s3 writes the findings report from the study in s2.
If the row is missing, the speech-language pathologist reads the paper topic list inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because a library colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Works-council consultation for a recording or scoring tool is out of scope because this design adds none.
Conducting the research stays in s2 at full time, and writing the report stays in s3 at full time.
unknowns: Whether this library already keeps a one-line topic card for each study.
research_questions: How often a first study has no row on the topic card.

incremental.description: No extra pathologist upkeep. A library colleague keeps the topic card.
A library colleague writes the topic card: topic title, shelf, and report date.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The study is the first one, so the topic card has no row and the pathologist reads the paper topic list. The search saving disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The speech-language pathologist still communicates with the student and still conducts the research and writes the findings report. A card only shortens finding the method or the topic.
reach: An occupational therapist reads the method card and still works with the student in the room.
An audiologist reads the topic card and still judges the hearing sources.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper method list or the paper topic list when the card has no row.
Decide the conversation and the findings from the student and the sources, not from the card.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not communicate or conduct research. The speech-language pathologist still does.
